questions.text: What is the most important starting point for developing personal Time Intelligence?
options: Creating a strict timetable for every hour
Understanding how beliefs, choices and constraints shape time use
Downloading a productivity application
Increasing the number of tasks completed daily

questions.text: Someone believes they must respond immediately to every request, even when it disrupts important activities. Which factor is most directly influencing their time use?
options: Their available weekly hours
Their personal belief about availability
Their technical productivity skills
Their physical working environment

questions.text: Which example best illustrates a realistic constraint rather than an avoidable time habit?
options: Repeatedly checking notifications without a purpose
Attending a scheduled medical appointment for a dependent
Opening social media whenever a task feels difficult
Revisiting the same email without taking action

questions.text: How many hours are available in a standard seven-day week?
options: 144 hours
160 hours
168 hours
176 hours

questions.text: A person spends 56 hours sleeping, 45 working and commuting, 30 on care and household duties, and 17 on personal care. How many hours remain?
options: 15 hours
20 hours
25 hours
30 hours

questions.text: Why is it misleading to assume that all hours remaining after fixed commitments are freely usable?
options: Because every remaining hour must be assigned to work
Because available time may still contain recovery, unpredictable needs and other responsibilities
Because discretionary time cannot be measured
Because personal planning is only useful during working hours

questions.text: Which statement most accurately distinguishes being busy, productive and effective?
options: Busy means producing outcomes, while effective means working longer
Productive means completing the largest number of tasks regardless of value
Busy refers to activity, productive to useful outputs, and effective to meaningful outcomes
All three terms measure the same aspect of time utilisation

questions.text: A learner spends two hours reading and can now explain a difficult concept accurately. Which is the clearest example of an outcome?
options: Opening the textbook
Spending two hours reading
Completing the assigned chapters
Demonstrating improved understanding

questions.text: A project manager attends six meetings, sends 40 emails and updates a tracker, but a critical decision remains unresolved. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: The manager has been effective because many activities were completed
The manager was active and produced an output, but the intended outcome remains incomplete
The manager was unproductive because no work was performed
The manager should eliminate all meetings immediately

questions.text: Which example is most clearly a recurring time leak?
options: Taking a necessary rest break
Providing essential care to a family member
Repeatedly searching for misplaced files because no consistent storage method exists
Attending a required appointment

questions.text: An avoidable interruption takes 12 minutes and happens three times daily over five working days. What is the weekly time cost?
options: 60 minutes
120 minutes
180 minutes
240 minutes

questions.text: What is the main purpose of using a Five Whys investigation on recurring time losses?
options: To identify who should be blamed for delays
To establish a deeper cause behind the recurring problem
To calculate the total number of hours in a week
To ensure that every task is completed more quickly

questions.text: Which sequence best represents the habit loop described in Week 1?
options: Outcome → deadline → schedule → reward
Cue → response → short-term effect → long-term pattern
Priority → delegation → performance → promotion
Planning → measurement → reporting → evaluation

questions.text: A notification arrives while someone is completing an important personal task. What is the best application of the 30-second decision filter?
options: Open the notification automatically
Ignore every notification without considering its importance
Check whether the interruption is essential or genuinely time-sensitive before deciding
Abandon the current task and reorganise the entire day

questions.text: Which approach is most appropriate when trying to replace an unhelpful daily habit?
options: Remove the habit without identifying what triggers it
Set an unrealistic target to create pressure
Identify the trigger, choose a useful replacement and monitor the change
Depend entirely on motivation to avoid the behaviour

questions.text: Why should personal roles and responsibilities be considered when planning time?
options: Because professional tasks should always take priority
Because realistic plans must account for care, health, relationships, work and other commitments
Because every role should receive exactly the same number of hours
Because responsibilities can always be removed through better planning

questions.text: A person faces a client deadline, a fixed school collection time and an optional social event. Which response best reflects Time Intelligence?
options: Accept every commitment and compensate by removing sleep
Protect essential responsibilities, assess consequences and negotiate or reschedule flexible commitments
Cancel school collection because work is always more important
Choose whichever activity feels easiest

questions.text: Which statement is the most effective way to communicate limited capacity?
options: I will try to do everything, although I cannot promise any result
Your request is unreasonable, so I will not consider it
I can complete the first task by Friday; the second would need Monday
I am too busy to discuss priorities

questions.text: The Week 1 Time Intelligence Diagnostic contains 24 statements across six dimensions, scored from 1 to 5. What is the possible total score range?
What is the most appropriate action after completing the Week 1 diagnostic?
options: Treat the score as a permanent measure of personal ability
Compare scores competitively with other participants
Identify patterns, choose one realistic improvement and review progress
Immediately attempt to change every aspect of time use

questions.text: Amara says improving her health is a major personal priority, but she repeatedly schedules optional activities during her planned exercise time. What should she do first?
options: Stop accepting all invitations indefinitely
Review whether her calendar choices reflect her stated values
Increase exercise intensity to compensate for missed sessions
Wait until she has a less demanding month

questions.text: Daniel has four goals: maintaining his health, supporting his children, developing a professional qualification and attending optional networking events. Which is the strongest basis for deciding how to allocate his limited time?
options: Choose whichever activity has the earliest invitation
Give equal time to all four goals regardless of circumstances
Consider personal values, consequences, deadlines and available capacity
Prioritise the goal that other people praise most

questions.text: A person has only one free hour this evening. They can either complete a course assignment due tomorrow or reorganise a cupboard that is already functional. What is the best choice?
options: Complete the assignment because it has a meaningful deadline and consequence
Reorganise the cupboard because it is easier to finish
Spend half an hour planning each task without starting either
Postpone both until the weekend

questions.text: Which task belongs in the ‘important but not urgent’ quadrant of the Eisenhower Matrix?
options: Responding to a time-critical safety concern
Completing a long-term savings plan before any immediate deadline
Responding to an unsolicited promotional message
Fixing an essential payment error due today

questions.text: A professional has a certification examination in six weeks. They repeatedly delay studying because no assignment is due this week. What is the main prioritisation mistake?
options: Confusing low urgency with low importance
Treating the examination as an emergency
Delegating too much preparation
Overestimating the value of daily breaks

questions.text: A participant has a medical appointment, a nonessential social invitation and a personal project milestone on the same afternoon. What is the most appropriate first step?
options: Cancel the medical appointment automatically
Accept all three and rely on multitasking
Assess which commitments are fixed, flexible and consequential
Choose the invitation received most recently

questions.text: Rita spends her mornings answering low-priority messages, leaving no time for a meaningful personal learning goal. Which change is most useful?
options: Check messages more frequently to clear them faster
Reserve a realistic learning period before routine message checking
Stop responding to all messages permanently
Extend every day by working late into the night

questions.text: A friend asks you to help organise an event during the only evening you have reserved for an important family commitment. What is the most constructive response?
options: Agree immediately to avoid disappointing your friend
Decline without any explanation or alternative
Explain your existing commitment and offer another realistic form of support if possible
Cancel the family commitment because helping others is always more important

questions.text: You are considering an optional weekend course that costs £200 and requires 12 hours. What is its opportunity cost?
options: Only the £200 course fee
Only the 12 hours spent attending
The value of the best alternative use of the money and time
The number of people who do not attend the course

questions.text: A participant accepts a new volunteer role despite already struggling with work, care responsibilities and recovery time. What is the most likely prioritisation risk?
options: The new role automatically becomes the highest priority
Adding a commitment without considering what it displaces may undermine existing priorities
Volunteering can never support personal values
Personal responsibilities should always be delegated

questions.text: A learner must choose between two valuable activities. One supports a long-term qualification; the other supports a short-term personal goal. Neither has an immediate deadline. What is the best decision method?
options: Always choose the shorter activity
Compare alignment with values, expected impact and realistic timing
Always choose the more expensive activity
Avoid making a decision until one becomes urgent

questions.text: A participant repeatedly says yes to requests because they fear appearing unhelpful. Which underlying issue should they examine?
options: Whether every request is objectively urgent
Whether approval-seeking is overriding their personal priorities and boundaries
Whether they should remove every personal commitment
Whether other people have more free time

questions.text: Which statement best demonstrates an effective personal boundary?
options: I will do everything you ask, but I may be exhausted
I cannot review this today; I can give it proper attention on Thursday
Your priorities are not important to me
I will respond whenever you remind me repeatedly

questions.text: Someone has committed to three optional evening activities but needs more time for rest and an important personal goal. Which strategy is most appropriate?
options: Reduce or decline one lower-value activity after reviewing the commitments
Keep every activity and reduce sleep
Assume the problem will disappear without making changes
Replace the personal goal with more social activities

questions.text: A person spends 40 minutes each day reviewing promotional emails they rarely use. Which action best fits the ‘eliminate’ decision?
options: Move the activity to a different time of day
Ask someone else to review every message
Unsubscribe from unnecessary promotional lists
Extend the activity to one hour

questions.text: A participant has a task that matters but does not require their personal involvement. Another capable person has agreed to handle it. Which decision is most suitable?
options: Eliminate the task regardless of its importance
Delegate the task with a clear expected result and deadline
Defer the task indefinitely
Continue doing the task personally to retain control

questions.text: A planned home improvement is useful but not time-sensitive, and the person is currently managing an unusually demanding month. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Treat it as an emergency
Defer it to a specific later review date
Remove essential rest to complete it immediately
Ignore the task permanently

questions.text: A person has to choose between an urgent request from someone else and a previously scheduled important personal commitment. What should they assess before changing plans?
options: Whether the requester sounds confident
The actual urgency, consequences and available alternatives
Whether the request arrived by phone or email
Whether the personal commitment is enjoyable

questions.text: Which approach best describes a useful personal priority hierarchy?
options: A permanent ranking that can never change
A list based entirely on what other people expect
An ordered guide reflecting values, essential responsibilities and current circumstances
A timetable that allocates identical hours to every role

questions.text: At the end of Week 2, which result would best demonstrate improved Priority Intelligence?
options: Having a calendar filled with activities
Being able to justify choices, protect meaningful commitments and adjust lower-value demands
Completing every request received from other people
Avoiding all unplanned situations

questions.text: A person has six hours available on Saturday but feels mentally exhausted after a demanding week. What is the most accurate assessment of their capacity?
options: They have six hours of fully productive capacity
They should use all six hours for unfinished work
Their available time exceeds their current usable energy and attention
Their exhaustion proves they have managed time poorly

questions.text: Nadia notices she can think clearly in the morning but struggles with demanding tasks late in the evening. What should she do?
options: Reserve cognitively demanding personal tasks for suitable high-energy periods
Force herself to complete every difficult task at night
Avoid planning because energy varies
Use her best hours exclusively for routine chores

questions.text: A parent works full-time, supports an elderly relative and is studying for a qualification. They feel unable to meet every commitment. What should they examine first?
options: How to eliminate sleep
Whether their combined commitments exceed realistic personal capacity
How to become constantly available
Whether they should abandon all personal goals

questions.text: Someone regularly schedules four demanding activities immediately after work but completes only one or two. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: Their plan may be based on unrealistic assumptions about available energy
They must lack ambition
They should double their schedule to increase motivation
Their unfinished activities have no value

questions.text: A participant feels physically energetic but mentally unable to concentrate after several hours of difficult decision-making. Which dimension is most likely depleted?
options: Financial capacity
Mental or cognitive capacity
Social capacity alone
Calendar availability

questions.text: A person has spent an emotionally demanding day supporting a family member. They still have two free evening hours. Which response best demonstrates Capacity Intelligence?
options: Assume emotional strain has no effect on performance
Schedule the most demanding tasks because the hours are available
Assess emotional energy and select a manageable activity or recovery
Cancel every future commitment permanently

questions.text: A learner has three important tasks but only enough capacity to complete one well today. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Begin all three simultaneously
Select the most consequential task and reschedule the others realistically
Work continuously until all three are finished
Choose whichever task is most enjoyable regardless of consequences

questions.text: Why is repeatedly accepting commitments without reviewing existing responsibilities risky?
options: It guarantees higher personal productivity
It may create capacity overload and undermine important commitments
It automatically improves time awareness
It eliminates the need for prioritisation

questions.text: A person consistently underestimates how long household and care responsibilities take. Which change would most improve their planning?
options: Stop recording these activities because they are not paid work
Use realistic time estimates based on previous experience
Assume future responsibilities will always take less time
Schedule personal development activities over every responsibility

questions.text: David has a major personal deadline tomorrow but has been sleeping poorly for several nights. What is the best immediate approach?
options: Ignore fatigue because the deadline is important
Assess essential work, reduce avoidable demands and protect necessary rest
Accept additional optional commitments
Continue without breaks until every task is finished

questions.text: A participant wants to exercise, study, spend time with family and maintain a demanding job. Which planning principle is most appropriate?
options: Allocate identical hours to each role every day
Build a realistic schedule that reflects essential duties, energy and changing needs
Treat personal wellbeing as optional
Assume every goal can progress at maximum intensity simultaneously

questions.text: A person says, ‘If I were more disciplined, I would never need a break.’ What is the most useful response?
options: Rest is evidence of weak motivation
Rest should be postponed until all responsibilities disappear
Recovery is a legitimate part of maintaining sustainable personal capacity
Discipline eliminates physical and mental limitations

questions.text: Someone notices that their concentration declines after a long period of focused work. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Introduce a suitable break and reassess their ability to continue
Ignore the decline and increase the workload
Add unrelated tasks to stimulate attention
Measure success only by the number of hours spent sitting

questions.text: A person is asked to take on a new voluntary responsibility during an already demanding month. Which response best protects personal capacity?
options: Agree immediately and decide later what to sacrifice
Explain current commitments and negotiate a smaller role or later start
Assume declining means they are selfish
Remove essential recovery time to accommodate the request

questions.text: Which example best demonstrates the difference between a boundary and avoidance?
options: Declining a nonessential request to protect an existing important commitment
Ignoring every difficult responsibility indefinitely
Refusing to discuss deadlines with anyone
Cancelling a necessary appointment because it feels inconvenient

questions.text: A participant plans three hours of study every evening but repeatedly manages only 45 focused minutes. What is the best adjustment?
options: Treat the entire week as a failure
Replace the plan with a sustainable study period and review progress
Increase the target to five hours to create pressure
Stop studying because the original target was missed

questions.text: A person has unpredictable caring responsibilities. Which strategy is most suitable for maintaining a personal learning goal?
options: Use only a rigid timetable with no alternatives
Create a primary study window and a smaller backup activity
Assume interruptions can always be prevented
Schedule every available minute without flexibility

questions.text: Someone feels guilty whenever they rest, even after completing essential responsibilities. Which belief would be most helpful to challenge?
options: Rest has value only when it produces immediate measurable output
Personal capacity is finite and recovery supports sustainable achievement
All free time should be used for additional commitments
Taking breaks means important goals are being abandoned

questions.text: A person is reviewing their week and discovers they completed important activities but experienced persistent exhaustion. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The week was successful, so no changes are necessary
Exhaustion should be ignored when tasks are completed
They should evaluate both outcomes and the sustainability of the effort required
They should increase next week’s workload automatically

questions.text: At the end of Week 3, which outcome best demonstrates improved personal Capacity Intelligence?
options: Accepting every opportunity presented
Completing more activities by reducing recovery time
Recognising personal limits, matching commitments to capacity and making sustainable adjustments
Maintaining a completely full calendar every day

questions.text: A learner has reserved an hour for an important personal qualification, but repeatedly checks messages whenever a difficult concept appears. What is the most likely underlying problem?
options: The qualification is no longer important
Mental discomfort is triggering an avoidable distraction
The learner needs to extend every study session
Messages are always more urgent than studying

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes attention from sustained concentration?
options: Attention selects what to engage with; sustained concentration maintains engagement over time
Attention and concentration both mean working quickly
Attention concerns only digital activities; concentration concerns reading
Concentration is determined entirely by the number of available hours

questions.text: A person is reading an important document when they suddenly remember an unrelated household task. What is the most effective response if the task is not urgent?
options: Immediately abandon the document
Try to remember the task while continuing to read
Record the task briefly and return to the document
Start several other tasks to clear their mind

questions.text: Someone is working in a noisy home environment and cannot concentrate. Which response best demonstrates personal Focus Intelligence?
options: Assume effective concentration is impossible at home
Identify controllable distractions and arrange a quieter or more suitable focus period
Increase the number of simultaneous tasks
Ignore every personal responsibility for the rest of the day

questions.text: A participant switches between writing an application, checking social media and responding to messages every few minutes. What is the main risk?
options: Switching automatically increases the quality of every task
Frequent switching creates reorientation demands and can reduce sustained attention
The participant will necessarily finish all tasks earlier
Task-switching has no effect unless the activities are professional

questions.text: A person believes that watching an educational video while writing a complex assignment is always an efficient use of time. What should they consider?
options: Whether both tasks require competing attention and reduce comprehension or writing quality
Whether they can increase the video’s volume
Whether the assignment can be completed without any review
Whether every minute contains at least two activities

questions.text: A learner takes 40 minutes to complete a task when uninterrupted, but repeatedly takes much longer while checking notifications. Which action would best test the impact of interruptions?
options: Stop measuring time altogether
Compare similar tasks completed with and without notifications under reasonably comparable conditions
Assume every notification causes exactly the same delay
Increase notification frequency during the next session

questions.text: A participant receives frequent nonessential notifications during personal study time. Which change is most suitable?
options: Disable or silence nonessential notifications during a defined study period
Delete every communication application permanently
Respond to every alert immediately to prevent a backlog
Leave all notifications active to build discipline

questions.text: A person reaches for their phone automatically whenever they feel bored. Which intervention addresses the habit most directly?
options: Move the phone out of immediate reach and choose a deliberate response to boredom
Buy a second phone for study periods
Check the phone more frequently before starting work
Assume the habit will disappear without changes

questions.text: Someone needs to remain reachable for an elderly relative while studying. What is the best digital-boundary approach?
options: Turn off every communication channel without exception
Keep every social-media alert enabled
Allow essential contacts through while silencing nonessential interruptions
Abandon studying whenever the relative might need help

questions.text: A participant plans a two-hour focus session but usually loses concentration after 30 minutes. What is the most realistic starting strategy?
options: Use shorter focused intervals with suitable breaks and adjust based on experience
Force two uninterrupted hours regardless of fatigue
Stop attempting important tasks
Measure success only by remaining seated for two hours

questions.text: Which example best demonstrates a useful pre-focus routine?
options: Open several unrelated applications before beginning
Define one intended result, prepare materials and remove avoidable interruptions
Wait until motivation becomes perfect
Begin without deciding what task matters

questions.text: A learner repeatedly rereads the same paragraph without understanding it after a demanding day. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Continue reading indefinitely to prove commitment
Assess fatigue, take a suitable break or choose a less demanding activity
Increase background distractions
Assume the material is impossible to learn

questions.text: A person wants to improve concentration but shares a home with young children. Which focus strategy is most realistic?
options: Expect complete silence throughout the day
Agree on suitable focus windows where possible and create a backup plan for interruptions
Treat all childcare interruptions as unnecessary
Schedule all demanding tasks without considering family responsibilities

questions.text: A participant keeps agreeing to optional calls during their only available learning period. What is the most effective boundary?
options: Accept every call and study after midnight
Communicate a reasonable period of unavailability and offer another suitable time
Ignore all contacts permanently
Cancel the learning goal because others need attention

questions.text: A person frequently interrupts their own focused activity to complete small unrelated tasks. What would be a useful improvement?
options: Create a brief capture list and review the unrelated tasks after the focus period
Complete every new task immediately
Avoid recording tasks because this wastes time
Extend the focus period each time an interruption occurs

questions.text: A participant wants to evaluate whether a new focus routine is working. Which measure provides the most useful evidence?
options: The number of applications installed on their phone
The number of hours they intended to concentrate
Completion and quality of meaningful tasks, alongside interruption patterns and wellbeing
The total number of messages received each day

questions.text: A learner has followed a focus routine successfully for four days, but a family emergency disrupts the fifth. What should they do next?
options: Consider the routine a failure and abandon it
Ignore the family emergency to preserve the routine
Respond to the emergency and restart the routine when realistically possible
Double the next session regardless of personal capacity

questions.text: Someone is deciding whether to work in a café, library or at home. What is the strongest basis for choosing a focus environment?
options: Choose the location that appears most productive on social media
Choose whichever location has the most people
Consider task demands, distractions, accessibility, cost and personal concentration patterns
Assume the same environment is ideal for every task

questions.text: At the end of Week 4, which outcome best demonstrates improved personal Focus Intelligence?
options: Never experiencing distraction again
Completing multiple demanding tasks simultaneously
Recognising attention triggers, reducing avoidable interruptions and returning deliberately to meaningful tasks
Working continuously without breaks

questions.text: A person has wanted to improve their financial knowledge for six months but has not started. Which action would best close the gap between intention and execution?
options: Keep reminding themselves that financial knowledge is important
Choose a specific 20-minute learning activity and schedule when to begin
Wait until they have enough time to complete an entire course
Set several additional financial goals before taking action

questions.text: A learner writes ‘I will become more productive’ as a weekly goal. What is the main weakness of this intention?
options: It is too focused on personal improvement
It does not identify a specific, observable action
It should include more than one outcome
It requires professional supervision

questions.text: Someone wants to update their CV but repeatedly postpones it because the entire task feels overwhelming. What is the best first step?
options: Wait until they can complete the whole CV in one sitting
Open the current document and update one recent responsibility
Start applying for jobs without reviewing the CV
Create a much longer list of everything that needs improvement

questions.text: A participant avoids contacting a training provider because they fear receiving an unfavourable response. Which factor most likely explains the delay?
options: Lack of available technology
Emotional avoidance linked to uncertainty or fear
Insufficient calendar space in every situation
The absence of a long-term goal

questions.text: A person repeatedly edits the opening paragraph of a personal statement but never completes a full draft. Which procrastination pattern is most evident?
options: Recovery-related delay
Perfectionism-related delay
Delegation-related delay
Scheduling-related delay

questions.text: A learner delays studying after several nights of poor sleep and substantial caring responsibilities. What should they assess before labelling the behaviour procrastination?
options: Whether the task could be made more difficult
Whether genuine fatigue and limited capacity explain the delay
Whether other learners are studying longer
Whether they can eliminate all future responsibilities

questions.text: A person notices that whenever an important task becomes uncomfortable, they open social media and feel temporarily relieved. What is the most effective intervention?
options: Recognise the avoidance trigger and begin a small, manageable part of the task
Increase social media use until the discomfort disappears
Wait for complete confidence before returning to the task
Remove the important task from every future plan

questions.text: Someone has repeatedly postponed writing an important email. Which implementation intention is strongest?
options: I will write the email when I feel ready
I will try to write more emails this week
After breakfast tomorrow, I will open my laptop and draft the first three sentences
I will think positively about sending the email

questions.text: A participant uses the first-15-minutes method to start a difficult task. Which approach best reflects its purpose?
options: Spend the entire period designing a perfect schedule
Clarify the immediate result, make a rough start, continue briefly and identify the next step
Complete the whole task regardless of its complexity
Use the time to compare every possible approach before acting

questions.text: A person has to make a difficult enquiry but cannot control whether the answer will be positive. Which measure of execution is most appropriate?
options: Whether the other person agrees with the request
Whether the person sends a clear, respectful enquiry
Whether the response arrives immediately
Whether the outcome exceeds their expectations

questions.text: A participant wants to complete an online qualification within three months. Which plan is most actionable?
options: Study whenever time becomes available
Set a final deadline without identifying intermediate steps
Identify module milestones, schedule realistic learning sessions and review progress
Spend the first month researching alternative qualifications

questions.text: Someone wants to improve their physical fitness but has an unpredictable weekly schedule. What is the most sustainable execution plan?
options: Commit to an identical demanding workout every day
Create a realistic primary activity and a smaller alternative for disrupted days
Avoid planning any physical activity
Increase the target whenever a session is missed

questions.text: A learner has three personal goals but continually switches between them without completing meaningful steps. What should they do?
options: Add two more goals to increase motivation
Define a next action and realistic milestone for each goal, then choose what to pursue first
Spend equal time on all goals regardless of importance
Stop recording progress until all goals are completed

questions.text: A participant successfully studies for four days but misses the fifth because of a family emergency. Which response best supports consistency?
options: Consider the entire routine unsuccessful
Double the next session regardless of fatigue
Resume with a realistic next action when circumstances allow
Abandon the learning goal until the following year

questions.text: Someone has set a daily 45-minute reading target but repeatedly manages only 10 focused minutes. Which adjustment is most appropriate?
options: Treat every shorter session as worthless
Define a realistic minimum reading action and gradually review what is sustainable
Increase the target to 90 minutes
Stop reading until a completely free day appears

questions.text: A participant wants to establish a regular personal reflection habit. Which approach is most likely to support follow-through?
options: Depend entirely on remembering the activity
Connect a brief reflection to an existing routine and establish a backup option
Change the reflection time randomly every day
Make the activity compulsory even during genuine emergencies

questions.text: A person submits three applications but receives no positive response. Which interpretation best reflects healthy personal accountability?
options: The effort has no value because the outcomes were unfavourable
They should examine the quality of their applications, recognise completed actions and refine their approach
They must submit applications continuously without reviewing them
The result proves they cannot achieve their goal

questions.text: During a weekly execution review, someone notices that a planned activity was repeatedly postponed. What is the most useful question?
options: Why am I incapable of following plans?
Which barrier affected the activity, and what adjustment would make the next action realistic?
How can I schedule more activities next week?
How can I avoid reviewing this commitment again?

questions.text: Which set of measures gives the clearest picture of personal execution?
options: Hours spent planning and number of reminders received
Actions completed, useful outputs, meaningful outcomes and learning
Number of activities listed in a diary
Total time spent thinking about goals

questions.text: At the end of Week 5, which outcome best demonstrates improved Execution Intelligence?
options: Having ambitious intentions for every area of life
Completing every task without experiencing discomfort
Turning meaningful goals into manageable actions, beginning consistently and adapting when circumstances change
Maintaining a completely full daily schedule

questions.text: After completing five weeks of Time Intelligence training, a participant wants to create a sustainable personal system. What should they do first?
options: Copy a successful person’s daily timetable
Combine their insights about time, priorities, capacity, focus and execution into a realistic personal approach
Schedule every available hour with an activity
Concentrate exclusively on completing more tasks

questions.text: A participant has improved their planning but continues to accept commitments that exceed their available energy. Which dimension requires particular attention?
options: Time awareness alone
Personal capacity and commitment management
Digital focus settings only
The number of calendar applications used

questions.text: A person knows which activities matter most but repeatedly becomes distracted when trying to complete them. Which combination of skills would be most useful?
options: Priority Intelligence and Focus Intelligence
Time awareness and financial planning
Calendar design and longer working hours
Delegation and social networking

questions.text: A parent works irregular shifts, has caring responsibilities and wants to study for a qualification. Which weekly planning method is most appropriate?
options: Use an identical timetable every week regardless of shift patterns
Plan around fixed commitments, realistic energy levels and flexible study windows
Study only when every other responsibility has disappeared
Schedule all free hours for study without recovery

questions.text: A participant creates a weekly plan containing 168 hours of activities, leaving no unallocated time. What is the main weakness?
options: The plan does not include enough productive tasks
The plan assumes that unexpected needs, transitions and recovery require no flexibility
The plan contains too many personal goals
The participant has not selected a calendar colour

questions.text: Someone wants to protect time for an important personal goal while maintaining essential family responsibilities. What is the strongest planning approach?
options: Give the personal goal priority over every family obligation
Identify essential commitments and reserve achievable periods for the goal
Wait until all family responsibilities end
Allocate the same number of hours to every responsibility

questions.text: A participant discovers that they regularly underestimate travel, preparation and transition time. What should they change?
options: Remove travel and preparation from the calendar
Add realistic estimates and suitable buffers based on previous experience
Schedule more activities to increase efficiency
Assume transitions will become faster automatically

questions.text: Which daily planning routine best supports personal Time Intelligence?
options: Create a long task list without ranking anything
Identify one meaningful outcome, choose a clear next action and allow for essential responsibilities
Begin with whichever task appears easiest and continue randomly
Spend the entire morning planning without starting

questions.text: A participant has maintained a useful daily routine for two weeks but finds that their weekly goals are drifting. What additional practice would help?
options: A brief weekly review of progress, priorities and capacity
A longer daily task list
Eliminating every leisure activity
Changing all goals every morning

questions.text: What is the most useful purpose of a monthly Time Intelligence review?
options: To judge personal worth based on the number of completed tasks
To identify patterns, evaluate meaningful progress and adjust the personal system
To create a completely new system every month
To compare working hours competitively with others

questions.text: A person consistently checks social media during a scheduled learning period. Which architectural change would most directly support better focus?
options: Increase the duration of the learning period
Place the phone away, silence nonessential alerts and establish a clear starting routine
Add more applications to monitor screen time
Wait until distractions stop feeling attractive

questions.text: A participant frequently misses planned activities because of unpredictable caring responsibilities. Which approach is most sustainable?
options: Remove every personal development goal
Use a primary plan with smaller backup actions and flexible review points
Treat each interruption as a personal failure
Ignore caring responsibilities when planning

questions.text: A person has completed all planned activities for several weeks but feels persistently exhausted. What should their review prioritise?
options: Increasing next week’s commitments
Evaluating whether the current level of activity is sustainable and whether sufficient recovery is protected
Adding more detailed productivity tracking
Reducing every break to save time

questions.text: Which example best demonstrates continuous improvement in personal time management?
options: Following an ineffective routine because it was originally planned
Making one evidence-based adjustment, observing its effect and refining the routine
Replacing every habit simultaneously
Changing routines without recording what happened
